gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: She has a ___ Scottish accent that is hard to miss.
gaps.explanation: a strong accent is the standard collocation; 'heavy accent' and 'deep accent' are not used.

gaps.sentence: You are ___ a big risk if you invest all your money in one company.
gaps.explanation: take a risk means to do something that might have a bad result.

gaps.sentence: It's hard to ___ friends when you move to a new city.
gaps.explanation: make friends is the fixed expression for forming friendships.

gaps.sentence: They ___ a lot of business with companies in Asia.
gaps.explanation: do business with somebody is the fixed expression for commercial activity.

gaps.sentence: It took her years to ___ a living from her painting.
gaps.explanation: make a living means to earn enough money to live on.

gaps.sentence: I ___ a strange dream last night.
gaps.explanation: have a dream is the English collocation; 'see a dream' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.
